paragraphs: Social Explorer sells a subscription web application for community analysis, built so that data is acquired and processed before the customer arrives. The application couples a data library with an AI-enabled Data Navigator that takes natural-language questions and returns dataset-specific analysis. Output takes the form of maps, charts, tables, and reports, and data can be exported to Excel, CSV, PDF, PNG, SAS, or SPSS formats.

The mapping product, SE Research, covers location-based community data at every geographic level and is positioned for users without a data science background. A subscription includes a library of crime, demographic, economic, environmental, equity, health, housing, political, and transportation data drawn from public and private sources.

SE Transform, a data pipeline management product, launches as a managed service and is built on Apache Airflow infrastructure. SE AI is sold as a domain-specific data chat interface, with a conversational front end, an API layer, and an admin panel. The homepage says the customer base includes educational and research institutions, government agencies, non-profits, healthcare systems, and businesses.

quote.text: Most of the time spent on community analysis involves acquiring and processing data.
